title: Time Mastery: Productivity and Balance at Work
summary: A comprehensive seven-module journey that transforms how you manage time, energy, and attention at work. Learn to prioritize effectively, plan strategically, manage meetings and focus, prevent burnout, maintain work-life balance, build sustainable systems, and handle interruptions with grace. Create a productivity practice that serves both your career and your well-being.

modules.title: Module 1 • The Foundation: Understanding Time, Energy, and Attention
modules.overview: Welcome to your journey toward time mastery. Effective time management isn't about doing more—it's about doing what matters most, with the energy you need, and the focus required to excel. This program will transform how you think about productivity: from busyness to impact, from hours worked to results achieved, from exhaustion to sustainable performance. Great productivity isn't about perfection—it's about creating systems and habits that support both your professional success and your personal well-being.
takeaways: Time is finite, but impact is not: focus on what creates the most value.
Energy management matters more than time management: work with your natural rhythms.
Attention is your most valuable resource: protect it fiercely.
Productivity is personal: what works for others may not work for you.
exercises: Myth audit: Which productivity myths do you believe? Which ones are affecting your work? Write about how letting go of one myth could change your approach.
Energy tracking: Track your energy for 3 days. Note when you're high energy, low energy, most focused, most creative. What patterns do you notice?
Attention audit: Track your attention for one day. What distracts you? How often do you switch tasks? How much time do you spend in deep work? What's your biggest attention thief?
homework: Energy pattern mapping: Map your energy patterns for a full week. Identify your peak times, low times, and what activities align with each. Use this to plan next week's schedule.
Attention protection: Identify your top 3 attention thieves. This week, create one boundary or system to protect against each. Note the impact.
Foundation building: Choose one foundation skill to focus on this week: self-awareness, clarity, boundaries, or systems. Practice it daily and note what you learn.
Productivity philosophy: Write your personal productivity philosophy. What does productivity mean to you? What matters most? What are your non-negotiables?

modules.title: Module 2 • Strategic Prioritization: Doing What Matters Most
modules.overview: You can't do everything. The key to productivity isn't doing more—it's doing the right things. This module teaches you to prioritize strategically, focusing on what creates the most value. Great prioritization isn't about urgent vs. important—it's about understanding impact, value, and strategic alignment. You'll learn frameworks that help you make better decisions about where to invest your time. When you prioritize well, you don't just get more done—you get the right things done, and you create space for what matters most.
takeaways: Not everything is equally important: prioritize based on impact, not urgency.
Saying no is a productivity skill: every yes is a no to something else.
Strategic alignment matters: prioritize work that supports your goals and values.
Regular prioritization prevents overwhelm: review and adjust weekly.
exercises: Eisenhower Matrix practice: List 10 current tasks. Categorize them using the matrix. What percentage of your time goes to each quadrant? What would you like to change?
Impact assessment: List 5 recent tasks or projects. For each, assess: What was the impact? What was the time investment? What was the ROI? What patterns do you notice?
Saying no practice: Identify 3 things you've said yes to that you should have said no to. What would you say instead? Practice saying no gracefully.
homework: Weekly prioritization: This week, use the Eisenhower Matrix or impact-based framework to prioritize your work. Schedule your top priorities first. Note what changes.
Saying no practice: Practice saying no to 2–3 requests this week. Use the techniques from this module. Note how it feels and what you create space for.
Delegation audit: Review your current tasks. What can you delegate? What can you eliminate? Create a plan to delegate or eliminate 3 things this week.
Weekly planning ritual: Establish a weekly planning ritual. Do it every Friday or Monday. Use it to align priorities with time. Make it a habit.

modules.title: Module 3 • Focus and Deep Work: Protecting Your Attention
modules.overview: In a world of constant distractions, the ability to focus deeply is a superpower. This module teaches you to create conditions for deep work, protect your attention, and produce your best work consistently. Deep work—focused, uninterrupted work on cognitively demanding tasks—is where real value is created. But it requires intention, boundaries, and systems. You'll learn to eliminate distractions, create focus-friendly environments, build deep work habits, and protect the attention that drives exceptional results.
takeaways: Deep work creates disproportionate value: protect time for it daily.
Distractions are expensive: each interruption costs focus and time.
Environment matters: create spaces that support focus.
Focus is a skill: practice it like any other skill.
exercises: Deep vs. shallow audit: Track your work for 3 days. Categorize each activity as deep or shallow. What's your current split? What would you like it to be?
Distraction inventory: List your top 5 distractions. For each, create one strategy to eliminate or minimize it. Implement this week.
Time-blocking practice: Create a time-blocked schedule for next week. Include deep work blocks, shallow work blocks, and breaks. Protect the deep work blocks.
homework: Deep work blocks: Schedule 3 deep work blocks this week. Protect them. Use them for your most important work. Note what you accomplish.
Distraction elimination: This week, eliminate your top 3 distractions during deep work. Turn off notifications, close tabs, set boundaries. Note the impact on focus.
Deep work ritual: Create your deep work ritual. Same time, place, preparation, intention. Practice it 3 times this week. Refine based on what works.
Focus tracking: Track your deep work hours this week. How many? What did you accomplish? How did it feel? Use this to plan next week.

modules.title: Module 4 • Meeting Management: Making Meetings Work
modules.overview: Meetings consume huge amounts of professional time, but most are poorly run and unproductive. This module teaches you to lead effective meetings, participate productively, and eliminate unnecessary meetings. Great meetings drive decisions, build alignment, and create value. Poor meetings waste time, create frustration, and drain energy. The difference is learnable. You'll learn to design meetings for outcomes, facilitate effectively, participate productively, and say no to meetings that don't create value.
takeaways: Meetings should drive action: if there's no decision or outcome, question the meeting.
Preparation enables productivity: agendas and pre-work make meetings effective.
Time is valuable: respect it by starting on time, ending on time, and staying focused.
Not every discussion needs a meeting: use async communication when appropriate.
exercises: Meeting audit: Review your calendar for the past week. How many meetings? How many had clear purpose? Agenda? Outcomes? What percentage felt valuable?
Meeting decision practice: Look at next week's meetings. For each, ask: Does this need to be a meeting? What's the purpose? Who needs to be there? Could this be async?
Facilitation practice: If you lead meetings, practice the facilitation skills from this module. Start on time, keep on track, drive decisions, capture outcomes. Get feedback.
homework: Meeting optimization: This week, optimize 3 meetings: add purpose and agenda, reduce duration if possible, or suggest async alternatives. Note what changes.
Facilitation practice: Lead one meeting using the framework from this module. Prepare purpose and agenda, facilitate effectively, capture outcomes. Note what works.
Meeting declination: Practice saying no to 2–3 unnecessary meetings this week. Use the techniques from this module. Note what you create space for.
Meeting-free time: This week, protect at least one half-day for meeting-free deep work. Block it on your calendar. Defend it. Note the impact.

modules.title: Module 5 • Preventing Burnout: Sustainable Performance
modules.overview: Burnout is epidemic in modern work. This module teaches you to recognize burnout signs, prevent it proactively, and create sustainable work practices that support both performance and well-being. Sustainable performance isn't about working less—it's about working smarter: managing energy, setting boundaries, taking breaks, and creating systems that prevent exhaustion. You'll learn to recognize burnout early, implement recovery practices, set boundaries, and create work habits that support long-term success without sacrificing your health.
takeaways: Burnout is preventable: recognize signs early and take action.
Recovery is essential: rest isn't laziness, it's productivity maintenance.
Boundaries protect you: saying no is self-care, not selfishness.
Sustainable performance beats heroic effort: consistency over intensity.
exercises: Burnout self-assessment: Rate yourself on burnout signs: exhaustion, cynicism, reduced efficacy. Are you at risk? What signs do you notice?
Recovery audit: How much recovery do you get? Daily? Weekly? Periodic? What's missing? What would you like to add?
Boundary assessment: What boundaries do you have? Which are strong? Which are weak? What boundaries would you like to set?
homework: Recovery practices: This week, implement 3 recovery practices: daily breaks, weekend protection, or disconnection. Note how they affect your energy and performance.
Boundary setting: Set one new boundary this week. Communicate it clearly. Enforce it consistently. Note how it protects your time and energy.
Workload management: Review your current workload. What can you say no to? What can you delegate? Take one action to reduce workload.
Sustainable habits: Identify one unsustainable habit you want to change. This week, practice the sustainable alternative. Note the impact.

modules.title: Module 6 • Work-Life Balance: Integrating Life and Work
modules.overview: Work-life balance isn't about perfect separation—it's about integration that supports both your career and your life. This module teaches you to create boundaries, manage transitions, and build a life that includes meaningful work without consuming everything else. Balance looks different for everyone. The goal isn't a 50/50 split—it's creating a life where work and life support each other rather than compete. You'll learn to set boundaries, manage transitions, protect personal time, and create systems that support both professional success and personal fulfillment.
takeaways: Balance is personal: find what works for you, not what works for others.
Boundaries enable balance: clear limits protect both work and life time.
Transitions matter: rituals help you switch between work and life modes.
Integration beats separation: work and life can support each other.
exercises: Balance assessment: Rate your current balance across work, relationships, health, personal growth, and rest. What's working? What's not? What would you like to change?
Boundary audit: What boundaries do you have? Which are strong? Which are weak? What boundaries would support better balance?
Transition ritual design: Design your end-of-work and start-of-work rituals. What will you do? When? How will it help you switch modes?
homework: Balance definition: Define your ideal balance. What matters in each area? How much time and energy for each? Create a vision for your balanced life.
Boundary implementation: Set and enforce one new work-life boundary this week. Communicate it clearly. Note how it affects your balance.
Transition practice: Practice your transition rituals this week. End-of-work and start-of-work. Note how they help you switch modes.
Personal time protection: This week, protect one block of personal time completely. No work. Note how it feels and what it enables.

modules.title: Module 7 • Systems and Routines: Building Sustainable Productivity
modules.overview: This final module helps you integrate everything into sustainable systems and routines. You'll create your personal productivity system, build habits that support excellence, and develop practices that ensure continued growth. Productivity mastery isn't about perfect systems—it's about systems that work for you, that you can maintain, and that support both your professional success and personal well-being. You'll design your productivity system, establish routines, build habits, and create a practice that supports long-term success.
takeaways: Systems beat willpower: good systems make good choices automatic.
Routines reduce decision fatigue: automate recurring decisions.
Habits compound: small daily practices create significant results.
Personalization matters: adapt systems to fit your style and needs.
exercises: System design: Design your productivity system. What components will it have? How will you plan, prioritize, execute, and review? Keep it simple.
Routine creation: Create one daily routine and one weekly routine. What will you do? When? How will it support your productivity?
Habit planning: Identify 3 productivity habits you want to build. How will you start? How will you track? How will you maintain?
homework: System implementation: Implement your productivity system this week. Use it daily. Note what works and what needs adjustment.
Routine practice: Practice your daily and weekly routines this week. Be consistent. Note how they support your productivity.
Habit building: Start building one productivity habit this week. Start small. Be consistent. Track your progress.
System review: At the end of the week, review your system. What's working? What's not? What will you adjust? Make one improvement.

aiSupport.systemPrompt: Help the user apply one concrete module step at a time. Do not diagnose. Escalate urgent safety concerns to emergency care.
